summary:
AGNIWATCH is a web-based wildfire hotspot monitoring platform that transforms NASA satellite observations into an interactive global visualization. It combines a rotating 3D Earth, satellite-detected thermal anomaly locations, and observation details in a unified dashboard.

The platform retrieves global fire and thermal anomaly records through the NASA FIRMS data service using a Python Flask API. Users can explore hotspot locations, inspect available satellite and sensor information, and examine patterns through dashboard filters and analytics.

By making satellite observations easier to visualize and understand, AGNIWATCH aims to support environmental awareness, research, and situational understanding of wildfire activity. Its interactive 3D interface makes complex geospatial information more accessible and engaging. AGNIWATCH is designed as an awareness and exploration tool; satellite detections require further verification and should not be treated as confirmed fire reports.
details: AGNIWATCH is an interactive web-based global wildfire hotspot monitoring system. It retrieves near-real-time active fire and thermal anomaly observations from NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) through a Python Flask backend API. The frontend is developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js powering the interactive 3D Earth visualization. Satellite-detected hotspot coordinates are displayed on the globe, allowing users to explore their geographical distribution. The dashboard also presents observation metadata, including satellite, sensor, confidence and fire radiative power where available. Filters and analytics help users explore the available records. The backend is deployed as a web service and the frontend as a public static website using Render. The project aims to make satellite-derived wildfire information easier to access, explore and understand for environmental awareness, education and research.
